Four wetlands hearings -- Mopus Road, Summer Street, a Northfield Road culvert, and Fire Road 15A -- were continued to January 7 for more information.

Two hearings were continued to September 3: Ashley Owens's 68A Laurel Lane project, missing its NOI number, and Tanner Cole's common driveway, pending peer review.
The Commission also approved several driveway, septic, wall, deck and tree-removal projects in wetland buffer zones, and issued negative determinations for a well and a deck project.
Two certificates of compliance and one tree-removal request were left unresolved, pending agent follow-up or a site visit before the next meeting.

why_it_matters: The Lake Wham approval sets a five-year plan for herbicide use near the town beach, with notice to residents handled through the town website and social media rather than a mailed abutter list.
Wetland buffer-zone approvals for driveways, septic systems, walls and tree removal show how the Commission conditions rather than blocks routine residential projects near water.
Two properties (68A Laurel Lane, Tanner Cole's driveway) and two certificates of compliance remain undecided, affecting those owners' pending work.

The board created an associate-commissioner slot (to be filled after outgoing member Mary Wilson's term ends), approved a small purchase for the pollinator habitat, and discussed process issues (a new interim conservation agent, default-continuation practice, notice timelines).

Approved, with conditions, a failed septic replacement on Northfield Road, a well and water line on Round Road, a rail right-of-way herbicide plan, and tree removal tied to a new house build.

Voted to create a new associate-commissioner seat, to be filled after outgoing member Mary Wilson's term ends.
Approved a purchase for the pollinator habitat, plants and a string trimmer, paid from the habitat fund.

why_it_matters: Property owners near wetlands: the buffer rule was enforced against work already built, not waived after the fact, which sets the standard for anyone doing landscaping near a wetland or shoreline.
Anyone proposing shoreline tree clearing, including for solar, learned the current bylaw does not allow it without a regulation change.
Septic, well and rail-corridor permits were approved with conditions, the routine path most wetlands-area projects in town follow.

what_happened.line: The Commission continued the 157 Goodridge Street driveway hearing to January 22 so an abutter without a computer could attend in person.
The Commission approved the DNA Lunenburg stormwater notice of intent on the September plans, with no buffer-zone changes; one member abstained.
The Commission approved the 50 Pine Grove Road notice of intent, 4-0 with one abstention.
The Commission continued the 400 Lunenburg-Shirley Road amendment and the 390 Howard Street hearing to January 22.
The Commission approved two certificates of compliance, denied a third for 32 Pine Grove Road until stabilized, and voted to send a letter to the 10 Mass Ave owner.

why_it_matters: Three wetlands hearings stay open until January 22, so abutters on Goodridge Street, Lunenburg-Shirley Road and Howard Street still have a chance to be heard before a decision.

The commission's FY26 budget asks (continuing education, handbooks, a tax-mailing flyer, a Ledger ad) were set as direction to the agent with no vote, so they will reach the town budget as requests, not decisions.
